title: Wringer offered answers
description: A `wringer.choices.v1` document — `wringer.choices.yaml`, beside `wringer.spec.yaml`: for an open question that has a few obvious answers, two to four plain-language ways a person MIGHT answer it, each with the consequence of picking it and a tiny example (0.8.4, P1.11). Exists because runs 4 and 4B (2026-09-01) put a drafter's question in front of a product manager with nothing beside it but a blank line. OFFERS, NEVER ANSWERS: nothing here is recorded until a person picks one at the interview or types their own words, and what is recorded is always the choice's TEXT — a typed number selects a choice and the number itself is never written, because an index is an answer to a question that may be reworded later. A sibling file keyed by question id, because `wringer.spec.v1` is frozen and its question items are `additionalProperties: false`. Source, not evidence: nothing under `.wringer/` is written from it, no gate reads it, and it has no authority over anything. `wring spec --send` writes one from the drafted reply; a person may write the same file by hand and everything downstream is identical.

choices.description: The id of an open question in `wringer.spec.yaml` to the choices offered for it. A key naming a question the spec does not ask is refused by the loader. Absent, never empty: a file offering nothing is not written.

additionalProperties.description: Between two and four. One option is a default wearing a list, and offers never fall back to a default; more than four is a form, and the person the interview is for stops reading.

text.description: The option in plain language — what is RECORDED as the answer when a person picks it. Never a bare number: a typed number selects the Nth choice, so an option whose words are a number could not be told from a selection. Unique within its question.

consequence.description: One sentence: what picking this means for what gets built.

example.description: A tiny concrete instance of this option, so the person can tell the options apart without imagining them.
